_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4), written for Octail on the pattern of the Purpur egg: Mojang's own server jar from the version manifest (piston-meta, v2), the version file and the jar checked against Mojang's SHA-1s, latest (the newest release) by default and snapshots only when asked for, a version without a server jar fails the install, the eula flag (the panel asks the owner on the first start, nothing is pre-accepted), Java 25 to 8 images (newest first), Minecraft Java idle sleep, install sandbox defaults and resource hints.
name: Vanilla Minecraft
author: octail@meowgafactory.com
description: Mojang's own Minecraft Java server, without plugins or mods (data packs only). Downloaded from Mojang and checked against the SHA-1 Mojang publishes.

installation.script:
#!/bin/ash
# Vanilla Minecraft installation (Octail): Mojang's own server jar from Mojang's version manifest (piston-meta,
# version_manifest_v2.json). The version file is checked against the SHA-1 the manifest lists for it, and the jar
# against the SHA-1 the version file lists. "latest" is the newest release, "snapshot" the newest snapshot (or the
# newest release when that is newer). A version Mojang doesn't list, or one without a server jar (the old alpha and
# beta versions), fails the install instead of installing another one.
#
# Server files: /mnt/server
set -eu

MANIFEST_URL=https://piston-meta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest_v2.json
JAR="${SERVER_JARFILE:-server.jar}"
VERSION="${MINECRAFT_VERSION:-latest}"

fail() {
	echo "Install failed: $*"
	exit 1
}
get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 20 "$1"; }
fetch() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 20 -o "$2" "$1"; }

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

MANIFEST=$(get "${MANIFEST_URL}") || fail "can't reach Mojang's version manifest (${MANIFEST_URL})"
case "${VERSION}" in
"" | latest) VERSION=$(echo "${MANIFEST}" | jq -r '.latest.release // empty') ;;
snapshot) VERSION=$(echo "${MANIFEST}" | jq -r '.latest.snapshot // empty') ;;
esac
[ -n "${VERSION}" ] || fail "Mojang's version manifest named no latest version"
ENTRY=$(echo "${MANIFEST}" | jq -c --arg v "${VERSION}" '.versions | map(select(.id == $v)) | .[0] // empty')
[ -n "${ENTRY}" ] || fail "Mojang has no Minecraft ${VERSION}. The versions are listed in ${MANIFEST_URL}"
TYPE=$(echo "${ENTRY}" | jq -r '.type // empty')
DOC_URL=$(echo "${ENTRY}" | jq -r '.url // empty')
DOC_SHA1=$(echo "${ENTRY}" | jq -r '.sha1 // empty' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')
case "${DOC_URL}" in
https://*.mojang.com/*) ;;
*) fail "Mojang's version manifest gave an unexpected address for the file of ${VERSION}" ;;
esac
echo "${DOC_SHA1}" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{40}$' || fail "Mojang's version manifest gave no SHA-1 for the file of ${VERSION}"

# The version file: its SHA-1 is checked on the file as downloaded (a shell variable would drop its last newline).
rm -f version.json.download
fetch "${DOC_URL}" version.json.download || fail "can't download Mojang's file for ${VERSION}"
GOT=$(sha1sum version.json.download | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
if [ "${GOT}" != "${DOC_SHA1}" ]; then
	rm -f version.json.download
	fail "SHA-1 mismatch for Mojang's file for ${VERSION} (expected ${DOC_SHA1}, got ${GOT})"
fi
SERVER_URL=$(jq -r '.downloads.server.url // empty' version.json.download)
SERVER_SHA1=$(jq -r '.downloads.server.sha1 // empty' version.json.download | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')
JAVA=$(jq -r '.javaVersion.majorVersion // empty' version.json.download)
rm -f version.json.download
[ -n "${SERVER_URL}" ] || fail "Minecraft ${VERSION} has no server jar (Mojang published none for the old alpha and beta versions)"
case "${SERVER_URL}" in
https://*.mojang.com/*) ;;
*) fail "Mojang gave an unexpected download address for the Minecraft ${VERSION} server" ;;
esac
echo "${SERVER_SHA1}" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{40}$' || fail "Mojang lists no SHA-1 for the Minecraft ${VERSION} server"

echo "Installing the Minecraft ${VERSION} server (${TYPE}) as ${JAR}"
rm -f "${JAR}.download"
fetch "${SERVER_URL}" "${JAR}.download" || fail "the download of the Minecraft ${VERSION} server failed"
GOT=$(sha1sum "${JAR}.download" | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
if [ "${GOT}" != "${SERVER_SHA1}" ]; then
	rm -f "${JAR}.download"
	fail "SHA-1 mismatch for the Minecraft ${VERSION} server (expected ${SERVER_SHA1}, got ${GOT})"
fi
if [ -f "${JAR}" ]; then
	mv -f "${JAR}" "${JAR}.old"
fi
mv "${JAR}.download" "${JAR}"

echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} server installed (SHA-1 ${SERVER_SHA1} checked)."
if [ "${TYPE}" != "release" ]; then
	echo "Note: Minecraft ${VERSION} is a ${TYPE}, not a release. Back up the world first: a snapshot can change or break it, and a world opened in a snapshot may not load in a release again."
fi
case "${JAVA}" in
'') ;;
8) echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} runs on Java 8: pick the Java 8 (or Java 11) image on the Startup tab." ;;
1[0-7]) echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} needs Java ${JAVA}: pick the Java 17 image on the Startup tab (Java 21 works too)." ;;
1[89] | 2[01]) echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} needs Java ${JAVA}: pick the Java 21 (or Java 25) image on the Startup tab." ;;
2[2-5]) echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} needs Java ${JAVA}: pick the Java 25 image on the Startup tab (the default)." ;;
*) echo "Minecraft ${VERSION} needs Java ${JAVA}, newer than this egg's images: ask your host for a newer Java image." ;;
esac
echo "Accepting the Minecraft EULA (https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA) is the server owner's decision: the panel asks on the first start."

variables.name: Minecraft Version
variables.description:
The Minecraft version to install, such as 1.21.11: latest for the newest release, snapshot for the newest snapshot (back up the world first), or a snapshot by its name. A version Mojang does not have fails the install.

The Startup image must fit it: Java 25 for the newest releases, Java 21 for 1.20.5 to 1.21.x, Java 17 for 1.17 to 1.20.4, Java 8 or 11 before that. The install log names the Java version the Minecraft version needs.

variables.name: Server Jar File
variables.description: The name of the server jar file.
